subject: Planned: eastus3 rolling I/O firmware reconciliation and driver reconciliation
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlascloud.com>, AtlasCloud Eng Ops <engops@atlascloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Planned: eastus3 rolling I/O firmware reconciliation and driver reconciliation

Hi Lena / AtlasCloud Eng Ops team,

Were writing to let you know about a planned maintenance activity in eastus3 next week aimed at reconciling device I/O firmware and host driver variations weve observed during the last capacity shuffle. This is a rolling, low-impact window and is part of our ongoing stability program to reduce transient kernel errors and nvme device flakiness.

Summary
- What: Rolling I/O firmware reconciliation + coordinated driver compatibility checks and safe-swap where needed.
- Where: region eastus3 (subset of hostpools serving AtlasCloud tenancy - we will target non-critical pools first).
- When: 2026-12-03 01:00–07:00 UTC (6-hour window, staged across AZs).
- Expected user impact: brief reconnects for active real-time sessions (most requests will be routed to warm replicas). No persistent data loss expected.
- Why: Weve seen a small spike in ENI-level retries and nvme error counters in eastus3 after a recent driver mix; reconciliation aligns firmware and drivers to the tested baseline.

Planned steps (high level)
1) Stage hosts and warm KV caches.
2) Apply firmware reconciliation (non-disruptive when possible).
3) For hosts that require driver rebind, perform safe-swap + live restart of inference service with automatic fallback.
4) Post-checks and telemetry validation for 30 minutes before returning to full traffic.

What we need from AtlasCloud
- Please confirm if you have any scheduled batch jobs or long-running pinned sessions during that window. If so, reply with the job IDs and owners and well coordinate a narrow exemption or a staggered cutover.

Attached is the runbook excerpt well follow and a short checklist. Well post live progress and any rollback decisions to the incident channel listed below.

Related links: https://drive.redwood.com/ops/runbooks/eastus3-io-reconciliation
Ticket: INF-4821

If you have any concerns about KV cache persistence or specialized workloads (streaming low-latency RL agents), call out those sessions explicitly so we can plan pinning.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlascloud.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasCloud Eng Ops <engops@atlascloud.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:03:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Planned: eastus3 rolling I/O firmware reconciliation and driver reconciliation

Thanks Rafael,

Appreciate the heads up. Two quick questions:
1) We run a small set of customer-facing streaming agents that maintain long-lived WebSocket connections for up to 30 minutes — will those be reconnected automatically and will they lose in-flight context?
2) Do you support pre-warming KV caches on a per-tenant basis prior to cutover? Wed like to avoid cold-start latency for a tranche of traffic post-update.

We dont have any large batch jobs during that window, but those streaming agents are critical. I can provide session IDs if needed.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Reliability, AtlasCloud

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlascloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:12:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Planned: eastus3 rolling I/O firmware reconciliation and driver reconciliation

Hi Lena — great questions. Short answers first, details below.

1) WebSocket long-lived sessions: we will orchestrate graceful reconnects. Active connections will receive a service-level disconnect with a short backoff. Clients should re-auth and resume. For in-flight context, if you rely on ephemeral in-memory state on the host, that will be lost on hosts that go through a safe-swap. We recommend storing conversation state in the KV cache (which well try to preserve) or Redis-backed session store.

2) Per-tenant pre-warm: yes. We can stage a prioritized KV cache warm for AtlasClouds critical tenant slice in the first stage of the window; this will reduce post-maintenance tail latency. If you confirm a list of tenant IDs (or prefix), Dev can queue a pre-warm job.

Operational notes
- We will mark your tenant slice for prioritized warm and keep an extra warm pool for 45 minutes after the last host finishes.
- If a host requires a driver rebind that necessitates an ephemeral restart, our router will route new requests to warm replicas and drain existing connections for up to 60s.
- We have a rollback plan if error rates exceed the gate thresholds defined in the runbook.

Action items for AtlasCloud
- Reply with tenant prefixes to pre-warm by 2026-12-02 16:00 UTC.
- If you want preserved in-memory session semantics, lets schedule a short architecture call (15m).

References
- Runbook excerpt attached.
- Prewarm job example: Doc: https://drive.redwood.com/ops/runbooks/prewarm-samples

Rafael

Checklist for staging (internal)

- [x] Reserve warm pool + add 2 extra instances for validation.
- [x] Run firmware-compatibility dry-run on a shadow subset (30 hosts).
- [ ] Coordinate NVMe SMART health snapshot immediately before reconciles.
- [ ] Ensure PD/PM on-call is reachable (Jordan).
- [ ] Notify SRE rotation for rollback windows 01:00–03:00 UTC.

If AtlasCloud confirms tenant prefixes by EOD well perform the pre-warm during AWS maintenance window and start the first host group at 01:00 UTC. We will post live progress to #ops-eastus3 (internal slack).

— Hannah
